S1: Each experiment cell replays one 36-step trace three times, so the repetitions show repeatability, not variety.
S2: On both telecom cells the model wrote a value above 100 (alternate path) on more steps than reactive routing did (26 vs 22 steps on cell 7511, 32 vs 28 steps on cell 8336), so part of its delay gain may come from using the faster path more, not from better forecasts.
S3: UDP packet loss was 0% in every scored run because the 10 Mbps link slowed the sender instead of dropping packets; we did not verify that mechanism, so loss does not separate the modes.
S4: The controller logs contain repeated Python AttributeError lines and large numbers of 'using alt path' log lines after route flips (for example 1060 lines for one switch in one step of a quick run). We did not establish the cause. POX kept running and every run completed, and the same controller was used in all experiments, so modes are compared only with each other and absolute numbers are not claimed.
S5: We did not test whether the forecast's content matters: no experiment replaced the model with a simple forecast that has the same timing.
S6: The telecom data is from Milan, November 2013, scaled to a unitless load where 100 stands for the 10 Mbps primary link.
S7: On the synthetic data the model's forecasts did not beat reactive routing on mean delay (24.84 ms vs 9.75 ms).
S8: An attempt to improve the model (v2) caught more jumps (17 vs 11 pooled onset windows on validation) but raised calm false alarms (16 of 111 vs 4 of 110) and mean error (15.78 vs 15.00). It was not adopted under rules written before the run, and v1 remains the final model. The v2 attempt was designed after the v1 test results were known and was judged on a separate validation block.
S9: Jump (onset) recall is modest and can be reported only for the telecom cells with at least 10 onset windows; the windows overlap, so they are not independent samples.
S10: Training loss shows that training ran and converged. It is not a measure of forecast quality, because in v1 it was computed over every token of the training text, prompt and padding included.
S11: The forecasts used in the experiments came from one training run on a Colab T4 GPU. Run-to-run variation in training was not measured. A local re-run of 20 test windows with the same adapter matched the Colab forecasts on 89 of 120 values (largest difference 4.3); beyond that the effect of different GPUs was not measured, so numbers from different GPUs are not mixed.
S12: The test block was scored once and the model was not tuned on it.
S13: All routing results come from an emulated network (Mininet with POX), not a real network.
S14: Dataset: Telecom Italia Big Data Challenge, Milan, November 2013, Harvard Dataverse DOI 10.7910/DVN/EGZHFV; attribution and licence terms are in datasets/telecom_milan/NOTICE.md.
